x: In the recent Civil Service cross-country championship, Derrick Burfitt was placed 3rd, with Eric Herbert 7th, Jack Brown 9th and Rene Howell 11th.

In both events Belgrave were well to the fore, as in the senior event Ted Stimpson, Bill Lucas, Archie Bedford, Vern Blowfield, Eric Herbert, Jack Bragginton and Steve Charlton were well up, and Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor were in the lead in the junior race.
E. H. Herbert · 17.27 · A. J. Snoad · 17.36
Eric Herbert went next and, although on a rather short lap, which was not really suitable to his style of running, Eric did well to maintain our lead.
Walker and Bill Lucas running for us in the two-mile team race, we gained an easy win, with Eric Herbert in fifth place to complete our team.
Archie Bedford ran a good race to beat Pudicombe of S.L.H. in the 2 miles, with Eric Herbert in third place, and the final points position was :—Belgrave H., 33; South London H., 16; Leicester, 5.
Hudson 6th, Len Adams 5th, Eric Herbert 6th, Len Herbert 4th, Len Bishop 4th, with Eddie Short taking us into the lead on the 9th stage, for Chas.

Mike Stearman ran well to finish 5th and our lads packed well in the 'teens so that scoring 12 a side we came out on top by a comfortable margin. Placings and times of our members were as under:—1, Tooby, 30.4; 5, Stearman, 30.16; 7, Short, 30.32; 10, Taylor, 30.51; 12, E.
Notable absentees included previous winners in Vern Blowfield and Len Herbert, and we had Eric Herbert running in the Civil Service race on the same day.
Eric Herbert 15th, and Denis Brickwood 16th, and our sixth man was J. Masters 21st, and as this was the latter's first County race, he did very well and should improve with further experience.
Eric Herbert, making one of his rare appearances, proved that he is still running quite well by finishing ninth. Also taking part was Jack Braughton who has now become a first claim member.

Rather naturally there were new names in our team in Vic Blowfield, George Lucas, Stan Eales, Eric Herbert and Albert Frost. It is interesting to note that of our ten runners, six were past or future Internationals.
The two miles team race is easily won by the Bels. with a team of Bill Lucas (no. 31), Chas. Walker (30) and Eric Herbert (42).
Our condolences go to Gwynne and to his brother Eric. W.E.LUCAS and G.S.DOUBLEDAY, with warmest thanks to Eric Herbert for providing some of the above information.

Early in April a 27 strong field tackled the 5 mile road run where experience, in the shape of Arthur Penny, triumphed over men who were to make their names over the coming years – Lucas, Len and Eric Herbert, and one who became “Mr Athletics” himself, Les Cohen.
